title: DDIA 4 · STORAGE & RETRIEVAL
subtitle: Two engine families: log-structured (append, LSM) and page-oriented (update in place, B-tree). Analytics wants columns; search wants special indexes.
footer: Study notes on Designing Data-Intensive Applications, 2nd edition (Kleppmann & Riccomini). Read the book.

blocks.text: Old values pile up, so background compaction merges segments and keeps only the latest value per key.
A read checks the memtable, then SSTables from newest to oldest. Bloom filters skip files that can't contain the key, so reads cost more than writes.
~10 bits per key → ~1% false "maybe", never a false "no". Lets reads skip SSTables.
Updates overwrite the page in place, after writing to the WAL first so a crash mid-write can be repaired. A full page splits in two.

head: LSM-tree (Cassandra, RocksDB, HBase)
B-tree (Postgres, MySQL InnoDB)
rows: Faster: sequential appends, less write amplification
Slower: random page writes + WAL (each write ≥ 2 writes)
Slower: may check several SSTables (Bloom filters help)
Faster, predictable: one path root → leaf
Compaction competes with live traffic, so p99 spikes
Key may exist in many files, so locking is harder
Key in one place: easy range locks
Write-heavy: metrics, logs, chat, IoT, events

blocks.text: "Ad clicks are write-heavy and append-only, around 10k/sec, so an LSM-based store like Cassandra fits.
Values in one column look alike, so they compress very well. Vectorized CPU processing on top makes these scans 10–100× faster.
Object storage → Parquet → Iceberg/Delta (transactions, time travel) → catalog → many query engines.
Embed text so similar meaning = nearby vectors. IVF searches near clusters; HNSW walks a layered graph. Behind RAG.

items: "LSM-tree storage: writes are sequential appends to memtable + commit log, so write throughput is very high.
"How do you make this query fast?"
Name the exact index: "a composite index on (user_id, created_at DESC) turns it into a single index range scan."
Never on the OLTP primary. Use CDC or Kafka into a column store (ClickHouse, BigQuery, Druid).
Log the change before applying it. After a crash, replay the log. The same idea powers replication (Ch 5) and CDC (Ch 11).
